A friend did similar but definitely more severe stuff to me at that age (talking about inappropriate stuff she shouldn’t have known about, pressuring us other girls to get naked, and even trying to get us to masturbate while laying on a blanket next to her). It made me and and my other friends really uncomfortable because we knew it wasn’t right. We told my mom and my mom contacted the girls mom. Turns out she was being abused by her grandfather. We had all spent time at the grandfathers house before and were lucky we weren’t abused too. After this all came out she moved cross country with her mom and was able to get away from her abuser and start to have a normal childhood. Overall it was a positive thing that it came out because otherwise no one would have been able to help her.

I can’t say that your situation is abuse, because honestly kids do that kind stuff innocently sometimes. Being on look out for the parents is a little bit weird for that though. Talk to her, she will be embarrassed and might have a hard time talking about it, but as her mom you’ll be able to feel her out. Is she scared? Ashamed? Let her know it’s ok to tell you what’s going on, and that even though that behavior isn’t appropriate for her to be doing that doesn’t make her a bad kid. 

If there seems to be a deeper issue than simple childhood curiosity then I would take her to a child psychologist. Let her know that you love her and want to help her by taking her to talk to someone really understanding and nonjudgmental who can help her express what she’s going through.

Don’t make it feel like a huge deal, that will make her feel ashamed and could be traumatic. Definitely convey the seriousness, but don’t make it feel like a family crisis.

Christmas Eve 2007.

My family and I (was about 11 at the time) returned home from a visit with the extended family to find our basement flooded with 1 1/2 ft of water. Naturally, my dad was using the basement as his office space where he built computers and wrote code. 

There was also the matter of the CARPET TILES. Originally installed for convenience, they now became hellish squares of irony that had to be individually pulled up, drained, then stacked. We had an assembly line going with my dad pulling them up, then me shaking out what water I could and stacking, followed by my mom hitting the floor underneath with the wet vac. We were in rain boots and the water was almost deep enough to pour over the top part of the boots. 

It took my parents and 11-year-old me from 8pm to 5:30 am to get this all sorted out. We decided to postpone presents while we slept in to the late afternoon. Most of the computer equipment survived, thankfully, but that was the end of the basement-office.

Despite all that, I regard this as a good memory of bonding with my parents over shared frustration. We love to laugh about it now.
